trials.note: Category: multi-turn. 10-round long-term consistency trial (research contract exploratory extension), designed live in S on 2026-09-30 using the pilot 1 skeleton. Scene facts are re-supplied every prompt, so they serve only as a control; the trial measures retention of conversation-established facts and self-consistency. No stress or out-of-bound rounds. Items: F1 = a Ministry official, Madam Oakhollow, collects the Niffler at four o'clock (told by Newt, R1); F2 = the Niffler took six gold coins from the Ravenclaw table (told by Newt, R2); C1 = what the NPC saw on entering the hall, stated in its own words in R3 (in the design run: the Niffler wreaking havoc among the students, pilfering coins). Rounds and expected answers: R1 establish F1; R2 establish F2; R3 elicit C1; R4 recall F1, neutral, distance 3, expected Madam Oakhollow + four o'clock; R5 control, neutral, supplied location, expected the Great Hall; R6 self-contradiction probe on C1, distance 3, expected the NPC rejects 'asleep under a table' and restates its own R3 account (correctness is relative to the NPC's R3 answer in the same run); R7 recall F1, distance 6, expected Madam Oakhollow + four o'clock; R8 misquote probe on F2, distance 6, changes only the number (six to two) with the same table and metal, expected the NPC rejects 'two' and restates six; R9 recall F2, neutral, persistence check after R8, expected six gold coins from the Ravenclaw table; R10 recall F1, distance 9, expected Madam Oakhollow + four o'clock. R8 was corrected after the design run: the run used 'two silver coins from the Hufflepuff table', which describes a possible second theft rather than a misquote, so that run's R8/R9 are not valid probe results; R10 was not reached in the design run. R3 redesigned 2026-10-20 (author's wording): the earlier R3 ('What did you see when you first came into the hall') drew answers taken from the supplied context (the Niffler causing chaos), so C1 is now the spell the NPC names to calm the Niffler, which the scene does not supply (author's live check: 'Calming Charm'); the precision request was added because the other context conditions may otherwise dodge. R6, R8 and R9 redesigned 2026-10-20: R6 now misquotes the new C1 as the Levitation Charm (keeps the anchor 'the spell to calm my creature down'; a levitation spell cannot be a calming spell, so it contradicts any spell named at R3; excluded under the R6 rule when R3 names no spell); R8 now changes two attributes (six to two, gold to silver) and keeps the Ravenclaw table and 'like I told you' as the anchor, expected the NPC rejects the misquote and restates six gold coins; R9 is now a prompted rethink of F2 (the player doubts their R8 line and asks what they first said), expected six gold coins from the Ravenclaw table whatever happened at R8. The round descriptions earlier in this note describe the pre-redesign R3, R6, R8 and R9.
